segments: The tenth dynasty.
The Arab kings.
a capable warrior was needed,
who could stand against the Franks,
for behold, they had terrified the entire region.
And they pointed to Atabeg Zengi, the son of Qasim al-Dawlah Aq Sunqur,
who was the military governor (shihnah) of Wasit and Baghdad.
The Sultan consented,
and he gave a diploma (sigillion) to Zengi,
and sent him to Mosul.
And he went first and took control over Bawazij (Bayt Waziq?),
and from there he went to Mosul.
And Jawali went out to meet him,
and he gave him Rahbut,
and sent him there.
And this Zengi entered Mosul,
and he gave the governorship of the fortress to Salah Yaghisiyani,
and the judgeship of Mosul and of every territory over which he ruled, to the son of Shahrazuri and to his seed forever.
And Zengi captured Jazira, Erbil, Sinjar, Rahbut, Aleppo, Hamath, and Homs.
And in the year one thousand four hundred and thirty-eight,
1438 of the Greeks [1126–1127 AD],
Ghazi and Arab met each other again in battle,
and Arab was defeated.
And Ghazi pursued after him,
and plundered his tents.
And he went and encamped against Comana and Ankara,
and fought against them fiercely and took them,
and brought out his son Muhammad,
who had been imprisoned there by Malik Arab.
And again Arab gathered an army and encountered Ghazi,
and was defeated.
And when he fled to the Greeks, he perished,
and no report of him came forth.
And in the year one thousand four hundred and thirty-eight,
1438, Bohemond, son of Bohemond the Frank, came out from Rome,
and came and reigned over Antioch.
And dissension fell among the Franks,
and Joscelin raided the whole territory of Antioch.
Then their patriarch became angry,
and shut the doors of the churches,
and silenced the semantra and prayers,
until Joscelin restored all the plunder.
And in the year one thousand four hundred and thirty-nine,
1439 of the Greeks [1127–1128 AD],
when the fear of Joscelin fell upon the Arabs of Aleppo,
they agreed to give him twelve thousand dinars every year,
so that he would not oppress them.
Then those Turks of Aleppo bribed with gold certain Frankish servants of Joscelin,
and they gave Joscelin and six horsemen with him deadly poison to drink.
And those six died,
but Joscelin, by the care of God and the treatment of physicians, was saved;
and he killed those who gave him the drink, and their sons.
